newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS plans new provisioning method.
newsitem.headline: CS plans new provisioning method.

text.p: CS Holding said it has adopted a new credit risk management method which will shift the group away from provisioning for actual defaults and to a system of setting provisions for statistically expected credit losses.
As part of this transition to the new provisioning method, CS Holding will set aside 630 million Swiss francs as an extraordinary provision for credit risks.

In addition, a fluctuation reserve of 2.0 billion Swiss francs will be established with around 450 million francs coming from the reserve for general bank risks and around 1.55 billion francs being charged to the extraordinary profit loss account.
CS Holding said a further extraordinary provision of 600 million francs will be formed to cover its Vertika AG subsidiary, a unit set up to hold Credit Suisse's high-risk credit provisions.

In total, 450 million francs will be set aside for extraordinary depreciation, comprising 350 million for depreciation on bank premises constructed during the economic boom period and 100 million as a result of the harmonisation of depreciation practices on fixed assets within the group.

Finally, a reserve of 300 million will be created owing to the integration of the emerging market trading operations of CS First Boston into the new Credit Suisse First Boston, which is subject to Swiss law and therefore the Swiss supervisory authorities.
